value.rationale: The minimum number of failed incidences necessary to destroy an originally consensus-bound state is a natural robustness invariant for a canonical cage network. The sharp two-incidence threshold depends exactly on whether deleted flags share an endpoint, while every defective network has a larger total consensus basin. The three geometry-sensitive populations and opposite basin-set versus size behavior are new motivated finite structural information, rather than an arbitrary computation or mere relabeling.
